description.value: An fMRI study examining the neural correlates and time course of cognitive reappraisal while participants recalled previously encoded aversive images.

spans.text: The present fMRI study examined the neural correlates of reappraisal that took place as individuals recalled aversive images that they had encoded a week prior to the scan.

description.value: Eighteen young adults completed a pre-scan image-encoding session and a later fMRI scan session involving emotion regulation of recalled negative images.

spans.text: Informed consent was obtained from all participants in accordance with the Boston College Institutional Review Board.

model_settings.value: Voxelwise general linear models modeled event types either as 12-second blocks or as separate Instruction, Memory Onset, and Memory Elaboration events. Trial-by-trial recall reaction time was included as a parametric regressor for the onset phase, and the number of days between encoding and retrieval was included as a second-level covariate.

Stimuli were presented using the MacStim presentation software in white text (Arial 36-point font) on a black background.

instructions.value: Participants were instructed to cognitively reappraise the emotional intensity associated with the recalled image to feel a lesser reaction after a Decrease cue or a greater reaction after an Increase cue. After a Maintain cue, they were instructed to recall the image without attempting to change their emotional reaction. They indicated with a button press when they had the fully formed image in mind and then elaborated on its details.
